terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where Sefton's quote tests run with your expectations.

tasks.title: Expect the same value
tasks.description:
Implement `toBe(expected)` in `src/expect.js`.

- it returns quietly when `actual` and `expected` are the same value, as `Object.is` sees it, so `NaN` is the same as `NaN`
- otherwise it throws an `Error` whose message shows the expected value first and then the value it got, each written with `inspect()` from `node:util`, like `Expected 4500 but got 4050`

The check calls `expect(...).toBe(...)` on numbers, strings and objects of its own and reads what is thrown.
nextSteps: Run `node tests/quote.test.js` and read the failing lines.
Throw an `Error` with both values when they differ.
Run it again: only the bulk price test should fail, with a message that shows both prices.
hints: `toBe` asks one question: is this the very same value? For objects that means the same object, not one that looks alike.
`===` says `NaN` is not equal to itself. `Object.is` says it is. `inspect('5')` writes the quotes, so text and numbers look different in a message.
When `!Object.is(actual, expected)`, throw `new Error('Expected ' + inspect(expected) + ' but got ' + inspect(actual))`.

tasks.title: Expect equal objects and arrays
tasks.description:
Implement `toEqual(expected)` in `src/expect.js`. It works like `toBe`, but two arrays or two plain objects are equal when they hold equal values.

- objects: the same keys, in any order, and equal values under each key
- arrays: the same length and equal values at the same places
- values inside are compared the same way, all the way down
- an array never equals an object that is not an array, and `null` never equals an object
- anything else is compared as `toBe` does

When the values are not equal it throws an `Error` with the same message as `toBe`. The check compares objects and arrays of its own, including ones that differ deep inside, in their keys, or only in key order.
nextSteps: Write a small function `equals(a, b)` above `expect` that returns true or false.
Start with the case where the two are the same value.
Then handle two objects: compare their keys, then each value with `equals` again.
Run the file: the printed quote test should pass.
hints: An object can hold other objects, so the comparison has to call itself for the values inside. Each call handles one level.
`Object.keys` lists an object's own keys, and works on arrays too. Count them on both sides, and make sure every key of one is a key of the other. `Array.isArray` tells arrays apart from objects.

Return true if `Object.is(a, b)`. Return false unless both are objects and not null, and unless `Array.isArray(a) === Array.isArray(b)`. Then compare the key counts, and check every key with `Object.hasOwn(b, key) && equals(a[key], b[key])`.

tasks.title: Expect a function to throw
tasks.description:
Implement `toThrow(text)` in `src/expect.js`. Here `actual` is a function.

- it calls the function once and returns quietly when it throws anything
- when the function returns instead, it throws an `Error` with the message `Expected the function to throw`
- when `text` is given, the thrown error's `message` must include it; when it does not, it throws an `Error` like `Expected an error with 'Unknown item' but got 'Price missing'`, each written with `inspect()`

The check passes functions of its own that throw, throw a string, or return.
nextSteps: Remember whether it threw, and what.
After the `try`, throw your own error when it did not throw or the message is wrong.
Run the file: the unknown item test should pass.
hints: There are two different errors here: the one the function throws, which you expect, and the one you throw when the expectation fails. Keep them apart.
Anything thrown inside a `try` lands in its `catch`, including your own `throw`. If you throw your failure inside the `try`, your `catch` swallows it.
Catch into a variable, such as `thrown = { error }`, and do every check after the `try...catch`: first whether anything was thrown, then whether `thrown.error.message.includes(text)`.
